subject.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch

question: Should plugin-runtime callers be permanently denied `sessions.patch` access to every legacy ownerless session row?
rationale: Failing closed strengthens plugin isolation but intentionally stops a previously accepted workflow for persisted rows created before ownership stamping, so the upgrade contract requires maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve strict denial
options.body: Keep ownerless rows inaccessible to plugins and require a documented operator or non-plugin recovery path with upgrade proof.

options.title: Migrate legacy ownership
options.body: Define a one-time doctor or storage migration that resolves ownership before enforcing strict runtime denial.

options.title: Preserve temporary compatibility
options.body: Delay ownerless-row enforcement behind a named, time-bounded compatibility path with an explicit removal plan.

recommendation.title: Approve strict denial
recommendation.body: Keep ownerless rows inaccessible to plugins and require a documented operator or non-plugin recovery path with upgrade proof.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the current projection boundary and is the strongest available routing candidate for its runtime, storage, and upgrade contract.
